sources.title: Creating a cleaner Enfield - bringing back weekly bin collections
sources.verified_claim: Enfield announced an immediate review of waste operations with a view to restoring weekly recycling and general-waste collections and reported a 33% recycling rate against a 50% target. Review intent is not yet a guaranteed service configuration or parcel-capacity result.

sources.title: Rubbish and recycling collection policy
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's collection policy describes monitoring, recycling priorities, food waste and alternative collection arrangements where standard bins are unsuitable. Household collection policy does not establish development-site waste capacity.

sources.title: How to reduce your waste
sources.verified_claim: Enfield provides current waste-reduction and reuse routes including food-waste separation and recycling-centre use; resident guidance is operational context rather than planning evidence for a parcel.

sources.title: Waste Planning
sources.verified_claim: Havering states the adopted 2012 Joint Waste Plan remains part of the planning-policy suite while the replacement East London Joint Waste Plan was submitted for examination on 30 January 2026. The replacement is emerging, not yet adopted.

sources.title: Waste strategy and related documents
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth publishes its municipal waste strategy and related collection charter. Borough waste-service strategy does not establish collection design, storage or network capacity for the sample parcel.

sources.title: Waste policy
sources.verified_claim: City Hall links London waste policy to waste reduction, reuse, recycling and local management objectives under the London Environment Strategy and London Plan. Regional objectives are not parcel-specific facility capacity.

sources.title: Waste and recycling
sources.verified_claim: City Hall's current waste programme states zero-waste and recycling ambitions and works with boroughs on Reduction and Recycling Plans; programme targets do not prove a site's waste infrastructure readiness.

sources.title: East London Joint Waste Plan examination overview
sources.publisher: London Borough of Redbridge on behalf of East London boroughs
sources.verified_claim: The East London Joint Waste Plan was submitted on 30 January 2026 and is undergoing independent examination for soundness and legal compliance for Barking & Dagenham, Havering, Newham and Redbridge. Examination status is explicitly retained and is not treated as adoption.
